record.hypothesis: A bounded layout model compared decoder rows against the constraints of a direct texture write and a 256-byte-aligned staging copy. Four layouts were legal for the direct path; an offset-misaligned control was rejected. Every staging reconstruction produced the identical visible RGBA bytes. The useful observation is structural: an uploader need not blindly normalize every row into a 256-byte staging layout when the destination operation admits the decoder's existing stride. Physical upload cost remains unmeasured here.
